meta.parties: Nagahawatte Et Al. v. Wettesinghe Et Al

rules.statement: An heir or beneficiary can be added as a party to an action by an executor or administrator if it transpires that the addition of such an heir or other person interested is desirable, and this decision should not be based on section 472 but rather on equitable principles established in English law.
rules.supporting_quote: "That principle has been explained in a series of English cases. In 1737, in the case of Beckley v. Dorrington, referred to in 6 Ves. Jr. 749, it was said: 'There can be regularly no suit against the debtor, but by the executor, who has the right both in law and equity ....... . There must be collusion or insolvency or some special case . . o . . The Court will interfere if there is such special case as collusion or insolvency.'"
